claims.quote: Unless otherwise provided, all briefs, motions, objections, applications or other filings made during a proceeding before an Administrative Law Judge, and all requests for review by the Secretary's designee, shall be filed with the Administrative Law Judge.
claims.summary: Unless otherwise provided, all briefs, motions, objections, applications or other filings made during a proceeding before an Administrative Law Judge, and all requests for review by the Secretary's designee, shall be filed with the Administrative Law Judge.

claims.quote: Filing with the Secretary's designee.
claims.summary: Filing with the Secretary's designee.

claims.quote: And all briefs, motions, objections, applications or other filings made during a proceeding before the Secretary's designee shall be filed with the Secretary's designee.
claims.summary: All briefs, motions, objections, applications, or other filings made during a proceeding before the Secretary's designee must be filed with the Secretary's designee.

claims.quote: Papers filed with an Administrative Law Judge or Secretary's designee shall be accompanied by a certificate stating the name of each person served, the date of service, the method of service and the mailing address or facsimile telephone number to which service was made, if not made in person.
claims.summary: Papers filed with an Administrative Law Judge or Secretary's designee must be accompanied by a certificate stating the name of each person served, the date of service, the method of service, and the mailing address or facsimile telephone number to which service was made, if not made in person.

claims.quote: All briefs containing more than 10 pages shall, to the extent applicable, include a table of contents, an alphabetized table of cases, a table of statutes, and a table of other authorities cited, with references to the pages of the brief wherein they are cited.
claims.summary: All briefs containing more than 10 pages must include a table of contents, an alphabetized table of cases, a table of statutes, and a table of other authorities cited, with references to the pages of the brief wherein they are cited.

claims.quote: All original documents shall be filed with the Administrative Law Judge or Secretary's designee, as appropriate.
claims.summary: All original documents must be filed with the Administrative Law Judge or Secretary's designee, as appropriate.

claims.quote: Papers filed in connection with any proceeding shall: (i) Be on one grade of unglazed white paper measuring 8.5 × 11 inches, except that, to the extent that the reduction of larger documents would render them illegible, such documents may be filed on larger paper;
claims.summary: Papers filed in connection with any proceeding must be on one grade of unglazed white paper measuring 8.5 × 11 inches, except that, to the extent that the reduction of larger documents would render them illegible, such documents may be filed on larger paper.

claims.quote: (ii) Be typewritten or printed in either 10- or 12-point typeface or otherwise reproduced by a process that produces permanent and plainly legible copies;
claims.summary: Papers filed in connection with any proceeding must be typewritten or printed in either 10- or 12-point typeface or otherwise reproduced by a process that produces permanent and plainly legible copies.

claims.quote: (iii) Include at the head of the paper, or on a title page, the title of the proceeding, the name(s) of each respondent, the subject of the particular paper or pleading, and the file number assigned to the proceeding;
claims.summary: Papers filed in connection with any proceeding must include at the head of the paper, or on a title page, the title of the proceeding, the name(s) of each respondent, the subject of the particular paper or pleading, and the file number assigned to the proceeding.

claims.quote: (iv) Be formatted with all margins at least 1 inch wide;
claims.summary: Papers filed in connection with any proceeding must be formatted with all margins at least 1 inch wide.

claims.quote: (v) Be double-spaced, with single-spaced footnotes and single-spaced indented quotations;
claims.summary: Papers filed in connection with any proceeding must be double-spaced, with single-spaced footnotes and single-spaced indented quotations.

claims.quote: (vi) Be stapled, clipped or otherwise fastened in the upper left corner.
claims.summary: Papers filed in connection with any proceeding must be stapled, clipped, or otherwise fastened in the upper left corner.

claims.quote: All papers must be dated and signed by a member of the Office of Chief Counsel, or other counsel assigned by the General Counsel to represent the Director, or a respondent or respondent's representative, as appropriate.
claims.summary: All papers must be dated and signed by a member of the Office of Chief Counsel, or other counsel assigned by the General Counsel to represent the Director, or a respondent or respondent's representative, as appropriate.

claims.quote: A respondent who represents himself or herself shall sign his or her individual name and state his or her address and telephone number on every filing.
claims.summary: A respondent who represents himself or herself must sign his or her individual name and state his or her address and telephone number on every filing.

claims.quote: A witness deposition shall be signed by the witness.
claims.summary: A witness deposition must be signed by the witness.

claims.quote: The signature shall constitute a certification that: (A) The person signing the filing has read the filing; (B) To the best of his or her knowledge, information, and belief, formed after reasonable inquiry, the filing is well grounded in fact and is warranted by existing law or a good faith argument for the extension, modification, or reversal of existing law; and (C) The filing is not made for any improper purpose, such as to harass or to cause unnecessary delay or needless increase in the cost of adjudication.
claims.summary: The signature shall constitute a certification that the person signing the filing has read the filing, that the filing is well grounded in fact and is warranted by existing law or a good faith argument for the extension, modification, or reversal of existing law, and that the filing is not made for any improper purpose, such as to harass or to cause unnecessary delay or needless increase in the cost of adjudication.

claims.quote: If a filing is not signed, the Administrative Law Judge (or the Secretary's designee) shall strike the filing, unless it is signed promptly after the omission is called to the attention of the person making the filing.
claims.summary: If a filing is not signed, the Administrative Law Judge (or the Secretary's designee) shall strike the filing, unless it is signed promptly after the omission is called to the attention of the person making the filing.

claims.quote: Written orders or decisions issued by the Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee shall be served promptly on each respondent and the Director pursuant to any method of service authorized under paragraph (a) of this section.
claims.summary: Written orders or decisions issued by the Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee must be served promptly on each respondent and the Director pursuant to any method of service authorized under paragraph (a) of this section.

claims.quote: Service of such orders or decisions shall be made by the Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee, as appropriate.
claims.summary: Service of such orders or decisions shall be made by the Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee, as appropriate.

claims.quote: If the Director has reason to believe there has occurred a violation of any provision of parts 500 or 515 of this chapter or a violation of the provisions of any license, ruling, regulation, order, direction or instruction issued by or pursuant to the direction or authorization of the Secretary pursuant to parts 500 or 515 of this chapter or otherwise under the Trading With the Enemy Act, and the Director determines that further civil proceedings are warranted, the Director shall issue a Prepenalty Notice.
claims.summary: The Director must issue a Prepenalty Notice if there is a violation of certain provisions and further civil proceedings are warranted.

claims.quote: The Prepenalty Notice shall describe the alleged violation, specify the laws and regulations allegedly violated, and state the amount of the proposed monetary penalty.
claims.summary: The Prepenalty Notice must describe the alleged violation, specify the laws and regulations allegedly violated, and state the amount of the proposed monetary penalty.

claims.quote: The Prepenalty Notice shall inform the respondent of respondent's right to make a written presentation within the time prescribed in § 501.707 as to why the respondent believes there should be no finding of a violation or why, if the respondent admits the violation, a monetary penalty should not be imposed or why, if imposed, the monetary penalty should be in a lesser amount than proposed.
claims.summary: The Prepenalty Notice must inform the respondent of their right to make a written presentation within the time prescribed in § 501.707.

claims.quote: The Prepenalty Notice shall also inform the respondent that: (i) The act of submitting a written response by the respondent is a factor that may result in a lower penalty absent any aggravating factors; and (ii) If the respondent fails to respond to the Prepenalty Notice within the applicable 60-day period set forth in § 501.707, the Director may proceed with the issuance of a Penalty Notice.
claims.summary: The Prepenalty Notice must inform the respondent that submitting a written response may result in a lower penalty and that failure to respond within 60 days may lead to the issuance of a Penalty Notice.

claims.quote: The Prepenalty Notice shall inform the respondent of respondent's right, if a subsequent Penalty Notice is issued, to request an administrative hearing. The Director will not consider any request for an administrative hearing until a Penalty Notice has been issued.
claims.summary: The Prepenalty Notice must inform the respondent of their right to request an administrative hearing if a subsequent Penalty Notice is issued, and the Director will not consider such a request until a Penalty Notice has been issued.

claims.quote: The respondent shall have 60 days after the date of service of the Prepenalty Notice pursuant to § 501.705(a) to respond thereto. The response, signed and dated, shall be served as provided in
claims.summary: The respondent must respond within 60 days after the date of service of the Prepenalty Notice, and the response must be signed and dated.

claims.quote: (2) The failure to submit a response within the time period set forth in this paragraph (a), including any additional time granted by the Director, shall be deemed to be a waiver of the right to respond to the Prepenalty Notice.
claims.summary: Failure to submit a response within the time period set forth in this paragraph (a), including any additional time granted by the Director, shall be deemed to be a waiver of the right to respond to the Prepenalty Notice.

claims.quote: (1) In general. The response need not be in any particular form, but must be typewritten and contain the heading “Response to Prepenalty Notice” and the Office of Foreign Assets Control identification number shown near the top of the Prepenalty Notice. It should be responsive to the allegations contained therein and set forth the nature of the respondent's admission of the violation, or defenses and claims for mitigation, if any.
claims.summary: The response must be typewritten and contain the heading “Response to Prepenalty Notice” and the Office of Foreign Assets Control identification number shown near the top of the Prepenalty Notice. It should be responsive to the allegations contained therein and set forth the nature of the respondent's admission of the violation, or defenses and claims for mitigation, if any.

claims.quote: (i) The response must admit or deny specifically each separate allegation of violation made in the Prepenalty Notice. If the respondent is without knowledge as to an allegation, the response shall so state, and such statement shall constitute a denial. Any allegation not specifically addressed in the response shall be deemed admitted.
claims.summary: The response must admit or deny specifically each separate allegation of violation made in the Prepenalty Notice. If the respondent is without knowledge as to an allegation, the response shall so state, and such statement shall constitute a denial. Any allegation not specifically addressed in the response shall be, deemed admitted.

claims.quote: (ii) The response must set forth any additional or new matter or arguments the respondent seeks, or shall seek, to use in support of all defenses or claims for mitigation. Any defense the respondent wishes to assert must be included in the response.
claims.summary: The response must set forth any additional or new matter or arguments the respondent seeks, or shall seek, to use in support of all defenses or claims for mitigation. Any defense the respondent wishes to assert must be included in the response.

claims.quote: (iv) Financial disclosure statement requirement. Any respondent who asserts financial hardship or an inability to pay a penalty shall include with the response a financial disclosure statement setting forth in detail the basis for asserting the financial hardship or inability to pay a penalty, subject to 18 U.S.C. 1001.
claims.summary: Any respondent who asserts financial hardship or an inability to pay a penalty shall include with the response a financial disclosure statement setting forth in detail the basis for asserting the financial hardship or inability to pay a penalty, subject to 18 U.S.C. 1001.

claims.quote: (2) Settlement. In addition, or as an alternative, to a written response to a Prepenalty Notice, the respondent or respondent's representative may seek settlement of the alleged violation(s). See
claims.summary: In addition, or as an alternative, to a written response to a Prepenalty Notice, the respondent or respondent's representative may seek settlement of the alleged violation(s).

claims.quote: § 501.710. In the event of settlement prior to the issuance of a Penalty Notice, the claim proposed in the Prepenalty Notice will be withdrawn and the respondent will not be required to make a written response to the Prepenalty Notice. In the event no settlement is reached, a written response to the Prepenalty Notice is required pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section.
claims.summary: In the event no settlement is reached, a written response to the Prepenalty Notice is required pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section.

claims.quote: § 501.708 Director's finding of no penalty warranted. If after considering any written response to the Prepenalty Notice submitted pursuant to § 501.707 and any other relevant facts, the Director determines that there was no violation or that the violation does not warrant the imposition of a civil monetary penalty, the Director promptly shall notify the respondent in writing of that determination and that no civil monetary penalty pursuant to this subpart will be imposed.
claims.summary: If after considering any written response to the Prepenalty Notice submitted pursuant to § 501.707 and any other relevant facts, the Director determines that there was no violation or that the violation does not warrant the imposition of a civil monetary penalty, the Director promptly shall notify the respondent in writing of that determination and that no civil monetary penalty pursuant to this subpart will be imposed.

claims.quote: The Director promptly shall issue a Penalty Notice informing the respondent that, absent a timely request for an administrative hearing, the Director will impose the civil monetary penalty described in the Penalty Notice.
claims.summary: The Director must issue a Penalty Notice if a violation is determined and a monetary penalty is warranted.

claims.quote: The Penalty Notice shall inform the respondent: (1) Of the respondent's right to submit a written request for an administrative hearing not later than 30 days after the date of service of the Penalty Notice;
claims.summary: The Penalty Notice must inform the respondent of their right to submit a written request for an administrative hearing within 30 days.

claims.quote: (2) That in the absence of a timely request for a hearing, the issuance of the Penalty Notice constitutes final agency action;
claims.summary: The issuance of the Penalty Notice constitutes final agency action if a timely request for a hearing is not made.

claims.quote: (3) That, absent a timely request for a hearing, payment (or arrangement with the Financial Management Service of the Department for installment payment) of the assessed penalty must be made not later than 30 days after the date of service of the Penalty Notice;
claims.summary: The respondent must make payment or arrange for installment payment of the assessed penalty within 30 days if a timely request for a hearing is not made.

claims.quote: (4) That absent a timely request for a hearing, the respondent must furnish respondent's taxpayer identification number pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 7701 and that the Director intends to use such information for the purposes of collecting and reporting on any delinquent penalty amount in the event of a failure to pay the penalty imposed.
claims.summary: The respondent must furnish their taxpayer identification number if a timely request for a hearing is not made.

claims.quote: Either the Director or any respondent may, at any time during the administrative civil penalty process described in this subpart, propose an offer of settlement.
claims.summary: Either the Director or a respondent may propose an offer of settlement at any time during the administrative civil penalty process.

claims.quote: Any offer of settlement made by a respondent prior to the issuance of a Penalty Notice shall be submitted, in writing, to the Chief of Civil Penalties, Office of Foreign Assets Control, U.S. Department of the Treasury, 1500 Pennsylvania Avenue, NW., Washington, DC 20220.
claims.summary: A respondent must submit any offer of settlement prior to the issuance of a Penalty Notice in writing to the Chief of Civil Penalties.

claims.quote: Any offer of settlement made by a respondent after issuance of a Penalty Notice shall state that it is made pursuant to this section; shall recite or incorporate as a part of the offer the provisions of paragraphs (b)(5)(ii) and (b)(6) of this section; shall be signed by the respondent making the offer, and not only by his or her representative; and shall be submitted to the Chief Counsel.
claims.summary: A respondent must submit any offer of settlement after the issuance of a Penalty Notice, stating it is made pursuant to this section, incorporating the provisions of paragraphs (b)(5)(ii) and (b)(6), and being signed by the respondent.

claims.quote: The submission of any settlement offer does not provide a basis for adjourning or otherwise delaying all or any portion of the administrative civil penalty process.
claims.summary: The submission of a settlement offer does not provide a basis for adjourning or delaying the administrative civil penalty process.

claims.quote: Any respondent (or potential respondent in the case of a pending Prepenalty Notice) may request, in writing, that the Director withhold issuance of any such notice, or grant an extension of time to respond to any such Notice, for a period not to exceed 60 days for the exclusive purpose of effecting settlement.
claims.summary: A respondent may request, in writing, that the Director withhold issuance of a notice or grant an extension of time to respond to a notice for up to 60 days for the purpose of effecting settlement.

claims.quote: Upon mutual agreement of the Director and a respondent, the Administrative Law Judge may grant an extension of time, for a period not to exceed 60 days, for the exclusive purpose of effecting settlement.
claims.summary: The Administrative Law Judge may grant an extension of time, up to 60 days, for the purpose of effecting settlement upon mutual agreement of the Director and a respondent.

claims.quote: Where an Administrative Law Judge is assigned to a proceeding, the Director or the respondent may request that the Administrative Law Judge express his or her views regarding the appropriateness of the offer of settlement.
claims.summary: The Director or the respondent may request that the Administrative Law Judge express their views regarding the appropriateness of an offer of settlement.

claims.quote: A request for the Administrative Law Judge to express his or her views on an offer of settlement or otherwise to participate in a settlement conference constitutes a waiver by the party making the request of any right to claim bias or prejudgment by the Administrative Law Judge based on the views expressed.
claims.summary: A party making a request for the Administrative Law Judge to express views on an offer of settlement or participate in a settlement conference waives any right to claim bias or prejudgment by the Administrative Law Judge based on the views expressed.

claims.quote: By submitting an offer of settlement, a respondent making the offer waives, subject to acceptance of the offer: (A) All hearings pursuant to section 16 of the Trading with the Enemy Act (50 U.S.C. App. 16); (B) The filing of proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law; (C) Proceedings before, and a decision by, an Administrative Law Judge; (D) All post-hearing procedures; and (E) Judicial review by any court.
claims.summary: By submitting an offer of settlement, a respondent waives all hearings, filing of proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law, proceedings before an Administrative Law Judge, post-hearing procedures, and judicial review by any court, subject to acceptance of the offer.

claims.quote: By submitting an offer of settlement the respondent further waives: (A) Such provisions of this subpart or other requirements of law as may be construed to prevent any member of the Director's staff, or members of the Office of Chief Counsel or other counsel assigned by the General Counsel, from participating in or advising the Director as to any order, opinion, finding of fact, or conclusion of law to be entered pursuant to the offer; and (B) Any right to claim bias or prejud, the Director based on the consideration of or discussions concerning settlement of all or any part of the proceeding.
claims.summary: By submitting an offer of settlement, the respondent further waives provisions preventing staff or counsel from participating in or advising the Director on orders, opinions, findings of fact, or conclusions of law to be entered pursuant to the offer, and any right to claim bias or prejudgment by the Director based on discussions concerning the settlement.

claims.quote: If the Director rejects the offer of settlement, the respondent shall be so notified in writing and the offer of settlement shall be deemed withdrawn.
claims.summary: If the Director rejects the offer of settlement, the respondent shall be notified in writing, and the offer shall be deemed withdrawn.

claims.quote: The rejected offer shall not constitute a part of the record in any proceeding against the respondent making the offer, provided, however, that rejection of an offer of settlement does not affect the continued validity of waivers pursuant to paragraph (b)(5) of this section with respect to any discussions concerning the rejected offer of settlement.
claims.summary: The rejected offer shall not constitute a part of the record in any proceeding against the respondent making the offer, although the validity of waivers related to discussions concerning the rejected offer is unaffected.

claims.quote: No settlement offer or proposal, or any subsequent negotiation or resolution, is admissible as evidence in any administrative proceeding initiated by the Director.
claims.summary: No settlement offer, proposal, negotiation, or resolution is admissible as evidence in any administrative proceeding initiated by the Director.

claims.quote: A respondent may not reserve the right to request a hearing after expiration of the 30 calendar day period. A request for a hearing that is not made as required by this paragraph shall constitute a waiver of the respondent's right to a hearing.
claims.summary: A respondent may not reserve the right to request a hearing after the 30 calendar day period. Failure to request a hearing as required constitutes a waiver.

claims.quote: The request need not be in any particular form, but must be typewritten and contain the heading “Request for Agency Hearing”.
claims.summary: The request for a hearing must be typewritten and contain the heading 'Request for Agency Hearing'.

claims.quote: The request must include the Office of Foreign Assets Control identification number shown near the top of the Penalty Notice.
claims.summary: The request must include the Office of Foreign Assets Control identification number from the Penalty Notice.

claims.quote: It should be responsive to the determination contained in the Penalty Notice and set forth the nature of the respondent's defenses or claims for mitigation, if any.
claims.summary: The request should be responsive to the determination in the Penalty Notice and set forth the nature of the respondent's defenses or claims for mitigation.

claims.quote: The request must admit or deny specifically each separate determination of violation made in the Penalty Notice. If the respondent is without knowledge as to a determination, the request shall so state, and such statement shall constitute a denial. Any determination not specifically addressed in the response shall be deemed admitted.
claims.summary: The request must admit or deny each separate determination of violation in the Penalty Notice. If the respondent is without knowledge, they must state so, which constitutes a denial. Any determination not addressed is deemed admitted.

claims.quote: The request must set forth any additional or new matter or arguments the respondent seeks, or shall seek, to use in support of all defenses or claims for mitigation. Any defense the respondent wishes to assert must be included in the request.
claims.summary: The request must set forth any additional or new matter or arguments the respondent seeks to use in support of defenses or claims for mitigation. Any defense the respondent wishes to assert must be included.

claims.quote: The request must accurately state, for each respondent (if applicable), the respondent's full name and address for future service, together with current telephone and, if applicable, a facsimile machine number. If respondent is represented, the representative's full name and address, together with telephone and facsimile numbers, may be provided in lieu of service information for the respondent. The respondent or respondent's representative is responsible for providing timely written notice to the Director of any subsequent changes in the information provided.
claims.summary: The request must accurately state the respondent's full name, address, telephone, and facsimile number. If represented, the representative's information may be provided instead. The respondent or representative is responsible for providing timely written notice of any changes.

claims.quote: The respondent or respondent's representative, must sign the hearing request.
claims.summary: The respondent or their representative must sign the hearing request.

claims.quote: No later than 60 days after service of any hearing request, the Director shall acknowledge receipt and inform a respondent, in writing, whether an Order Instituting Proceedings shall be issued.
claims.summary: The Director must acknowledge receipt of a hearing request and inform the respondent in writing whether an Order Instituting Proceedings will be issued within 60 days.

claims.quote: The Director may, in his or her discretion, withdraw an Order Instituting Proceedings at any time prior to the issuance of a decision by the Administrative Law Judge.
claims.summary: The Director may withdraw an Order Instituting Proceedings at any time prior to the issuance of a decision by the Administrative Law Judge.

claims.quote: The Order Instituting Proceedings shall: (1) Be prepared by the Office of the Chief Counsel or other counsel assigned by the General Counsel and based on information provided by the Director; (2) State the legal authority under which the hearing is to be held; (3) Contain a short and plain statement of the alleged violation(s) to be considered and determined (including the matters of fact and law asserted) in such detail as will permit a specific response thereto; (4) State the amount of the penalty sought in the proceeding; and (5) Be signed by the Director.
claims.summary: The Order Instituting Proceedings must be prepared by the Office of the Chief Counsel or other counsel assigned by the General Counsel, based on information provided by the Director. It must state the legal authority, contain a short and plain statement of the alleged violation(s), state the amount of the penalty sought, and be signed by the Director.

claims.quote: The Director may combine claims contained in two or more Penalty Notices involving the same respondent, and for which hearings have been requested, into a single Order Instituting Proceedings.
claims.summary: The Director may combine claims from two or more Penalty Notices involving the same respondent, for which hearings have been requested, into a single Order Instituting Proceedings.

claims.quote: Upon motion by the Director, the Administrative Law Judge may, at any time prior to issuance of a decision, permit the Director to amend an Order Instituting Proceedings to include new matters of fact or law that are within the scope of the original Order Instituting Proceedings.
claims.summary: Upon motion by the Director, the Administrative Law Judge may permit the Director to amend an Order Instituting Proceedings to include new matters of fact or law within the original scope.

claims.quote: Not later than 45 days after service of the Order Instituting Proceedings, the respondent shall file, with the Administrative Law Judge and the Office of Chief Counsel, an answer to each of the allegations contained therein.
claims.summary: The respondent must file an answer to each allegation in the Order Instituting Proceedings within 45 days of service.

claims.quote: A respondent may file with an answer a motion for a more definite statement of specified matters of fact or law to be considered or determined.
claims.summary: The respondent may file a motion for a more definite statement of specified matters of fact or law.

claims.quote: A respondent may amend its answer at any time by written consent of the Director or with permission of the Administrative Law Judge.
claims.summary: The respondent may amend its answer at any time with written consent of the Director or permission of the Administrative Law Judge.

claims.quote: The respondent shall receive not less than 45 days notice of the time and place of the hearing.
claims.summary: The respondent shall receive at least 45 days notice of the time and place of the hearing.

claims.quote: Any respondent named in an order instituting proceedings as a person against whom findings may be made or penalties imposed who fails to appear (in person or through a representative) at a hearing of which he or she has been duly notified may be deemed to be in default pursuant to § 501.716(a).
claims.summary: A respondent who fails to appear at a hearing may be deemed in default.

claims.quote: If a respondent fails to file an answer required by this subpart within the time prescribed, such respondent may be deemed in default pursuant to § 501.716(a).
claims.summary: A respondent who fails to file an answer within the prescribed time may be deemed in default.

claims.quote: A party to a proceeding may be deemed to be in default and the Administrative Law Judge (or the Secretary's designee during review proceedings) may determine the proceeding against that party upon consideration of the record if that party fails: (1) To appear, in person or through a representative, at any hearing or conference of which the party has been notified; (2) To answer, to respond to a dispositive motion within the time provided, or otherwise to prosecute or defend the proceeding; or (3) To cure a deficient filing within the time specified by the Administrative Law Judge (or the Secretary's designee) pursuant to § 501.729(b).
claims.summary: A party to a proceeding may be deemed in default if it fails to appear at a hearing or conference, answer or respond to a dispositive motion, or cure a deficient filing within the specified time.

claims.quote: In deciding whether to determine the proceedings against a party deemed to be in default, the Administrative Law Judge shall consider the record of the proceedings (including the Order Instituting Proceedings) and shall construe contested matters of fact and law against the party deemed to be in default.
claims.summary: The Administrative Law Judge must consider the record of the proceedings and construe contested matters of fact and law against the party deemed to be in default.

claims.quote: All hearings shall be conducted in a fair, impartial, expeditious and orderly manner.
claims.summary: All hearings must be conducted in a fair, impartial, expeditious, and orderly manner.

claims.quote: Each party has the right to present its case or defense by oral and documentary evidence and to conduct such cross examination as may be required for full disclosure of the relevant facts.
claims.summary: Each party has the right to present its case or defense by oral and documentary evidence and to conduct cross-examination as required for full disclosure of relevant facts.

claims.quote: The Director shall present his or her case-in-chief first. The Director shall be the first party to present an opening statement and a closing statement and may make a rebuttal statement after the respondent's closing statement.
claims.summary: The Director must present his or her case-in-chief first and be the first party to present an opening statement and a closing statement, with the option to make a rebuttal statement after the respondent's closing statement.

claims.quote: From the time the Director issues an Order Instituting Proceedings until the date of final decision, no party, interested person, or representative thereof shall knowingly make or cause to be made an ex parte communication.
claims.affected_party: party, interested person, or representative thereof
claims.summary: Prohibition on making ex parte communications during proceedings.

claims.quote: Except to the extent required for the disposition of ex parte communication matters as authorized by law, the Secretary's designee and the Administrative Law Judge presiding over any proceeding may not: (i) Consult a person or party on an issue, unless on notice and opportunity for all parties to participate; or (ii) Be responsible to or subject to the supervision, direction of, or evaluation by, an employee engaged in the performance of investigative or prosecutorial functions for the Department.
claims.affected_party: Secretary's designee and the Administrative Law Judge presiding over any proceeding
claims.summary: Prohibition on consulting a person or party on an issue without notice and opportunity for all parties to participate, and being subject to supervision, direction, or evaluation by employees engaged in investigative or prosecutorial functions.

claims.quote: If an ex parte communication is received by the Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee, the Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee, as appropriate, shall cause all of such written communication (or, if the communication is oral, a memorandum stating the substance of the communication) to be placed on the record of the proceeding and served on all parties.
claims.affected_party: Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee
claims.summary: Requirement to place ex parte communication on the record and serve it on all parties.

claims.quote: A party may, not later than 10 days after the date of service, file a response thereto and may recommend that the person making the prohibited communication be sanctioned pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section.
claims.summary: Requirement to file a response within 10 days and recommend sanctions for prohibited communication.

claims.quote: Any party to the proceeding, a party's representative, or any other interested individual, who makes a prohibited ex parte communication, or who encourages or solicits another to make any such communication, may be subject to any appropriate sanction or sanctions imposed by the Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee, as appropriate, for good cause shown, including, but not limited to, exclusion from the hearing and an adverse ruling on the issue that is the subject of the prohibited communication.
claims.affected_party: party to the proceeding, a party's representative, or any other interested individual
claims.summary: Prohibition on making or encouraging prohibited ex parte communication, with potential sanctions.

claims.quote: Any officer or employee engaged in the performance of investigative or prosecutorial functions for the Department in a proceeding as defined in § 501.702 may not, in that proceeding or one that is factually related, participate or advise in the decision pursuant to Section 557 of the Administrative Procedure Act, 5 U.S.C. 557, except as a witness or counsel in the proceeding.
claims.affected_party: officer or employee engaged in investigative or prosecutorial functions
claims.summary: Prohibition on participating or advising in the decision in a proceeding or one that is factually related, except as a witness or counsel.

claims.quote: All hearings, except hearings on applications for confidential treatment filed pursuant to § 501.725(b), shall be public unless otherwise ordered by the Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee, as appropriate, on his or her own motion or the motion of a party.
claims.affected_party: Administrative Law Judge or the Secretary's designee
claims.summary: Requirement to make hearings public unless otherwise ordered.

claims.quote: The Administrative Law Judge may direct a representative or any party to attend one or more prehearing conferences.
claims.summary: The Administrative Law Judge may direct a representative or any party to attend one or more prehearing conferences.

claims.quote: Such conferences may be held with or without the Administrative Law Judge present as the Administrative Law Judge deems appropriate.
claims.summary: Such conferences may be held with or without the Administrative Law Judge present as the Administrative Law Judge deems appropriate.

claims.quote: Where such a conference is held outside the presence of the Administrative Law Judge, the Administrative Law Judge shall be advised promptly by the parties of any agreements reached.
claims.summary: Where such a conference is held outside the presence of the Administrative Law Judge, the Administrative Law Judge shall be advised promptly by the parties of any agreements reached.

claims.quote: The Administrative Law Judge shall enter written rulings or orders that recite the agreement(s) reached and any procedural determinations made by the Administrative Law Judge.
claims.summary: The Administrative Law Judge shall enter written rulings or orders that recite the agreement(s) reached and any procedural determinations made by the Administrative Law Judge.

claims.quote: A respondent who fails to appear, in person or through a representative, at a prehearing conference of which he or she has been duly notified may be deemed in default pursuant to § 501.716(a).
claims.summary: A respondent who fails to appear, in person or through a representative, at a prehearing conference of which he or she has been duly notified may be deemed in default pursuant to § 501.716(a).

claims.quote: A party who intends to call an expert witness shall submit, in addition to the information required by paragraph (b)(1)(iv) of this section, a statement of the expert's qualifications, a list of other proceedings in which the expert has given expert testimony, and a list of publications authored or co-authored by the expert.
claims.summary: A party who intends to call an expert witness must submit, in addition to the information required by paragraph (b)(1)(iv) of this section, a statement of the expert's qualifications, a list of other proceedings in which the expert has given expert testimony, and a list of publications authored or co-authored by the expert.

claims.quote: Unless the Administrative Law Judge orders otherwise, all disclosures under paragraphs (a) through (c) of this section shall be made in writing, signed, and served as provided in § 501.705.
claims.summary: Unless the Administrative Law Judge orders otherwise, all disclosures under paragraphs (a) through (c) of this section must be made in writing, signed, and served as provided in § 501.705.

claims.quote: Unless otherwise limited by order of the Administrative Law Judge in accordance with paragraph (f)(2) of this section, the scope of discovery is as follows: (1) In general.
claims.summary: Unless otherwise limited by order of the Administrative Law Judge in accordance with paragraph (f)(2) of this section, the scope of discovery is as follows: (1) In general.

claims.quote: Parties may obtain discovery regarding any matter, not privileged, that is relevant to the merits of the pending action, including the existence, description, nature, custody, condition, and location of any books, documents, or other tangible things and the identity and location of any persons having knowledge of any discoverable matter.
claims.summary: Parties may obtain discovery regarding any matter, not privileged, that is relevant to the merits of the pending action.

claims.quote: For good cause, the Administrative Law Judge may order discovery of any matter relevant to the subject matter involved in the proceeding.
claims.summary: The Administrative Law, Judge may order discovery of any matter relevant to the subject matter involved in the proceeding.

claims.quote: Respondent's interrogatories shall be served upon the Office of the Chief Counsel not later than 30 days after issuance of the Order Instituting Proceedings.
claims.summary: Respondent's interrogatories shall be served upon the Office of the Chief Counsel not later than 30 days after issuance of the Order Instituting Proceedings.

claims.quote: The Director's interrogatories shall be served by the later of 30 days after the receipt of service of respondent's interrogatories or 40 days after issuance of the Order Instituting Proceedings if no interrogatories are filed by respondent.
claims.summary: The Director's interrogatories shall be served by the later of 30 days after the receipt of service of respondent's interrogatories or 40 days after issuance of the Order Instituting Proceedings if no interrogatories are filed by respondent.

claims.quote: Parties shall respond to interrogatories not later than 30 days after the date interrogatories are received.
claims.summary: Parties shall respond to interrogatories not later than 30 days after the date interrogatories are received.

claims.quote: Interrogatories shall be limited to 20 questions only. Each subpart, section, or other designation of a part of a question shall be counted as one complete question in computing the permitted 20 question total. Where more than 20 questions are served upon a party, the receiving party may determine which of the 20 questions the receiving party shall answer.
claims.summary: Interrogatories shall be limited to 20 questions only. Each subpart, section, or other designation of a part of a question shall be counted as one complete question in computing the permitted 20 question total. Where more than 20 questions are served upon a party, the receiving party may determine which of the 20 questions the receiving party shall answer.

claims.quote: Privileged documents are not discoverable.
claims.summary: Privileged documents are not discoverable.

claims.quote: A party who has made an initial disclosure under paragraph (a) of this section or responded to a request for discovery with a disclosure or response is under a duty to supplement or correct the disclosure or response to include information thereafter acquired whenever: (1) The party learns that in some material respect the information disclosed is incomplete or incorrect, if the additional or corrective information has not otherwise been made known to the other party during the discovery process or in writing; or (2) Ordered by the Administrative Law Judge. The Administrative Law Judge may impose sanctions for failure to supplement or correct discovery.
claims.summary: A party must supplement or correct a disclosure or response if information is incomplete or incorrect, or if ordered by the Administrative Law Judge.

claims.quote: All discovery, including all responses to discovery requests, shall be completed not later than 20 days prior to the date scheduled for the commencement of the hearing, unless the Administrative Law Judge finds on the record that good cause exists to grant additional time to complete discovery.
claims.summary: All discovery and responses to discovery requests must be completed no later than 20 days before the hearing, unless additional time is granted by the Administrative Law Judge.

claims.quote: No witness may testify and no document or exhibit may be introduced at the hearing if such witness, document, or exhibit is not listed in the prehearing submissions pursuant to paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section, except for good cause shown.
claims.summary: Witnesses, documents, or exhibits not listed in prehearing submissions may not be introduced at the hearing unless good cause is shown.
